correction: docs/org-adrs.md recorded that snapshot.yml dispatches build to frostyard/snow (core ADR-0013). frostyard/snow had been renamed frostyard/snow-bootc, archived and marked Deprecated, and the continue-on-error 'Kickoff snow' step failed on every snapshot run checked (2026-08-19 to 2026-09-28) without failing the workflow. Image rebuilds are now dispatched by frostyard/apt-publisher after a tag release is published (core ADR-0056), and snapshot.yml dispatches nothing.
evidence: gh repo view frostyard/snow (name snow-bootc, archived, 'Deprecated'); 'Kickoff snow' step errors in snapshot runs 32284872244, 33163172585, 34913816701, 36475121875 and 36478845492; frostyard/core ADR-0056

correction: AGENTS.md documented `make test` as running `go test ./...`, and the frostyard-go-repo skill documents `make bump` as running build/test/fmt/lint before tagging. `test` was missing from `.PHONY`, so make treated the target as the top-level `test/` directory, reported it up to date and ran nothing; `make bump` tagged v0.11.2 without running the tests. Every Makefile target is now declared `.PHONY`, and a test enforces it.
evidence: `make test` on 3505e94 printed "make: 'test' is up to date." and exited 0; `make bump` printed "make[1]: 'test' is up to date." while tagging v0.11.2; internal/installcheck/makefile_phony_test.go

correction: ChairLift assumed that a nil error from updex Client.UpdateFeatures meant every enabled feature updated, and always showed 'Features updated. Changes apply after reboot.'. Since updex v2.1.0 a nil error also covers features the next-boot image gate holds (transfer NeedsImage or NotLinked, Installed=false) and features held by a rollback record. updex v2.1.3 can also return an error wrapping sysext.ErrActivationIncomplete (merged, activation unfinished), and a per-transfer failure returns the results together with the error. Only the per-feature results say what happened.
evidence: github.com/frostyard/updex/v2@v2.1.3 updex/features.go UpdateFeatures (NeedsImage/NotLinked/Held branches, 'return allResults, errors.Join(...)'), updex/results.go UpdateResult, sysext/runner.go ErrActivationIncomplete; chairlift PR #253

correction: ChairLift believed the unprivileged Features update check reported NeedsImage on bootc hosts. Reality: bootc status --json needs root, so updex's minimum image version gate erred on every component, and ChairLift's partitionFeatureChecks dropped those components, so the 'waiting for a newer OS image' row never appeared after a restart on a bootc host.
evidence: bootc status --json as uid 1001 on bootc 1.17.1 prints 'This command must be executed as the root user'; updex v2.1.3 imagecompat/bootc.go NextBootImageVersion falls back only on exec.ErrNotFound; internal/updex/partitionFeatureChecks drops component errors

correction: PR #261 believed the danglingSymlink check in Load made every dangling config symlink fail closed. Reality: resolveCandidatePath probed the executable-relative config.yml with os.Stat, so a dangling symlink there resolved to the working-directory file instead and Load fell through to it or to enabled defaults. The probe is now os.Lstat.
evidence: cross-review of frostyard/chairlift#261 at 471d36e5; internal/config.TestLoadDanglingExecutableRelativeSymlinkFailsClosed and the dangling subtest of TestResolveCandidatePathBranches fail with statPath = os.Stat

correction: PR #260 disabled Pango markup on toasts but no test guarded it: with window.go reverted, every test still passed. The change was unprotected because internal/window cannot host a test binary.
evidence: cross-review of frostyard/chairlift#260 at 6e51495e; internal/installcheck.TestToastsRenderPlainText now parses production Go files and fails when an adw.NewToast result is shown without SetUseMarkup(false)

correction: ChairLift believed a nil error from updex Client.Features meant updex features were configured, so updex.IsInstalled returned true on a host without feature definitions and the Features page showed an empty group with an active Update button. updex returns an empty slice with a nil error when no features are configured; IsInstalled now also requires len(features) > 0.
evidence: github.com/frostyard/updex/v2@v2.1.3 updex/features.go Client.Features ('if len(features) == 0 { ... return []FeatureInfo{}, nil }'); internal/updex.TestUpdexAvailabilityRequiresNonEmptyFeatures; ported from the bluefin chairlift fork (0f069c8e)

correction: PR #262 believed a scope-less `flatpak uninstall --unused` cleaned only the system installation and split it into --user and --system runs. Reality: flatpak parses uninstall with FLATPAK_BUILTIN_FLAG_ALL_DIRS, so the scope-less command already cleans the user, the default system and every extra system installation; the split dropped the extra installations.
evidence: flatpak app/flatpak-builtins-uninstall.c (ALL_DIRS flag, --unused loop over dirs) and app/flatpak-main.c (no scope flag selects user, system and installations.d dirs), tags 1.10.0, 1.14.0, 1.16.0; internal/flatpak.TestUninstallUnusedCoversEveryInstallation

correction: PR #262 believed the Flatpak update reload would always replace the clicked row, so the per-app button stayed at 'Updating...' after success. Reality: a reload in which both installation queries fail keeps the old rows, so the button stuck. The button now follows actionstate.PackageUpgrade: restore on failure or dry-run, remove the row and decrement the count on live success.

ChairLift treated a RemoteError from both Flatpak installations as a total failure even when each query returned healthy-remotes updates. Partial updates are now authoritative and publishable; only two failed installations with zero updates keep the last known rows and count.

PR #265 believed the Progress worker could run on its own after the window closed. Reality: the worker had no application hold and no close guard, so a close ended ChairLift while flatpak still ran and the completion markers were never written. The window now blocks close-request while Flow.CanClose is false and holds the application until the worker ends.

PR #265 believed a logged completion failure was enough. Reality: a ResolvePaths or MarkDone error left the Done step saying 'Your user account is ready to use'. Completion now carries Err and ShowWarning, and DoneState shows the warning and an error-log entry. The 'starts again at your next login' text shows only when no marker exists after the failure (DoneAt is false); a partial failure that left a marker shows 'Setup finished with errors'.
evidence: PR #265 cross-review and re-review 1; internal/firstrun.TestCompleteReportsMarkDoneFailure, TestCompleteAtReportsMissingConfigHome and TestCompletePartialFailureDoesNotPromiseAnotherRun

correction: PR #265 believed one gsettings goroutine per Style toggle was safe. Reality: the goroutines can finish out of order and leave the color scheme the user did not choose last. One SchemeWriter now writes serially and the latest choice wins.

PR #265 believed logging a configuration error was enough in the first-run window. Reality: AGENTS.md requires a configuration error to stay visible as a persistent toast. The first-run window now shows LoadError.ToastMessage in a toast with timeout 0 and markup off.

PR #265 believed a 0700 mode check on the config home proved MarkDone's directory mode. Reality: the test pre-created the config home with touch (0755), so the check passed only under a 077 umask and failed in CI (umask 022). The mode check now uses a fresh config home that only MarkDone creates, and the legacy autostart removal has its own test.
evidence: PR #265 CI (Unit Tests, Race Detection) at 60c7a28; internal/firstrun.TestMarkDoneWritesBothMarkersInPrivateDirectories and TestMarkDoneRemovesLegacyAutostart, run under umask 022 and 077

correction: PR #265 believed the serial SchemeWriter alone kept the last color-scheme choice. Reality: nothing drained it, so Progress could record completion, release the hold and show Exit while a write was pending, and Exit ended the process first. RunProgress now runs the actions, drains the writer (SchemeWriter.Wait), then records completion, on the worker goroutine.

PR #265 believed every completion error meant the first run starts again at the next login. Reality: MarkDone can fail after it wrote the markers (for example when the legacy autostart path is a non-empty directory), and the gate then skips the next login. DoneState now takes the gate state (DoneAt) and shows 'starts again' only when no marker exists, else 'Setup finished with errors'.
